title: openai-compat: refine tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting for function/tool calling
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compat function/tool calling layer closer to the OpenAI semantics (tool_choice, explicit schema mappings, and message formatting) while preserving backward compatibility and runtime stability. This PR implements a mapping layer that ingests OpenAI-style tool schemas and normalizes them to Redwood's internal tool descriptors, clarifies tool_choice handling (selection semantics vs. automatic invocation), and standardizes how tool outputs are formatted back into chat messages and streaming chunks. Key design points: 1) Schema mapper: canonicalizes types, required/optional fields, and nested objects into a flat validation schema used by the runtime; 2) tool_choice semantics: when a model returns a tool_choice, we now support both a) explicit selection (user intent to invoke tool) and b) ambiguous tool_hint (model suggests a tool but does not finalize invocation) — controlled by a compatibility flag; 3) Message formatting: tool outputs are wrapped as assistant messages with a consistent content-type header in streaming frames so clients can reliably detect tool output boundaries and structured payloads; 4) Backwards compatibility: new behavior is off by default for Hosted API; rollout will flip the feature-flag for internal canaries and Dedicated customers after validation. Checklist: - [x] schema mapper implementation and unit tests - [x] tool_choice state machine + feature-flag - [x] streaming formatting + e2e tests - [x] docs and SDK examples updated - [x] canary rollout plan included Changes: - Add src/compat/schema_mapper.py: implements OpenAI->Redwood schema translation and normalization rules - Add src/compat/tool_choice_handler.rs: state machine for tool_choice handling and compatibility flag gating - Add src/compat/message_formatter.ts: streaming chunk formatters and content-type header injection - Update runtime integration in src/runtime/openai_compat_integration.rs to call mapper/handler/formatter - Tests: tests/tool_choice_integration_test.py, tests/streaming_tool_output_test.ts - Docs: docs/openai_compat/tool-calling.md and examples/openai-compat/tool-call-usage.md Rollout plan: enable feature-flag in staging, run internal traffic (5%), enable in canary tenants (10%), monitor quality/regressions for 72h, then flip to opt-in for Hosted customers and notify Dedicated customers via release notes. Compatibility notes: the schema mapper intentionally simplifies deeply nested schemas by mapping nested objects to JSON blobs when ambiguous; SDKs should update to rely on typed validation where available. See release_notes below for migration steps.

Maya Chen: Concern about streaming chunk boundary semantics when tool output interleaves with assistant tokens. Are we preserving deterministic boundaries for clients?

release_notes: Improvements to OpenAI-compatible tool calling: schema mapping for tool definitions, clearer tool_choice semantics (compat flag), and more robust streaming formatting for tool outputs. Backwards compatible by default; SDKs should update to handle normalized schemas and streaming markers. See docs/openai_compat/tool-calling.md for migration steps.
notes_on_compatibility: Feature gated: existing hosted customers keep legacy behavior until opt-in. Dedicated/private deployments can opt into new semantics via feature flag. SDKs must be updated to recognize the 'tool-output' streaming frame marker; examples updated.
tests_and_coverage: Unit and integration coverage added for schema mapper, tool_choice state machine, and streaming formatter; e2e exercised via the new ci integration matrix and internal canary traffic.
